question.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=36.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $6$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 6,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =((\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2})\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{6}{\rho }^{5}{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$
